text_blocks.snippet: State and local officials warn that fake text messages about unpaid traffic tolls, DMV fees, and package deliveries are the most common active scams targeting Central Illinois residents.
Here are the top scams to watch out for and how to protect yourself:

list.snippet: Fake Traffic and Toll Violations: Scammers send text messages pretending to be the Illinois Secretary of State, DMV, or tollway system. These texts claim you owe unpaid fines and threaten license suspension if you do not pay immediately.

Package Delivery Texts: Fraudsters send text messages claiming a USPS, UPS, or generic delivery is stuck due to a missing address or fee. The texts include a link to steal your credit card or personal details.

Impersonation Scams: Con artists use AI or phone calls to pose as Federal Communications Commission (FCC) employees, tech support, or family members in distress, claiming your accounts are under criminal investigation or hacked.

Property Deed Fraud: Criminals target vacant land or homes without mortgages using quick-claim deeds to illegally take or sell property. Local recorder offices (like Champaign County) offer free alert programs for this.
Do Not Click Links: Government agencies and shipping carriers never send unprompted text messages demanding payment or personal info.
Practice the Pause: Take time to verify urgent claims through official websites or phone numbers rather than the contact info provided in the message.

Report Suspicious Texts: Forward fraudulent state-related texts to the official Illinois Scam Alert

reporting portal or contact the Illinois Attorney General
. You can also track local trends with the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois.
